blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Bookkeeping discipline, at the rise level, is about keeping the operation steady as the company grows. When a firm has ten transactions a day, almost anything works. When it has a thousand, only a real routine survives.

The routine is simple on paper. Record transactions daily, not weekly. Reconcile bank accounts at least every Friday. Close the books by the fifth working day of the following month. Document every exception. Store every supporting receipt where it can be found.

None of these steps is difficult on its own. All of them become hard when the volume grows and nobody has protected the routine. A good team head protects it politely but firmly — because once it slips, it takes months to rebuild, and the damage shows up on the audit report nobody wanted to write.

items.q: According to the text, what happens to a bookkeeping routine when a firm has only ten transactions a day?
items.why: "When a firm has ten transactions a day, almost anything works" — o problema só aparece com o volume.

items.q: By when should the books be closed each month?
options: By the fifth working day of the following month
By the last Friday of the month
By the end of the same month
items.why: "Close the books by the fifth working day of the following month."

items.q: According to the text, why do the routine steps become hard?
options: Because volume grows and nobody protects the routine
items.why: "All of them become hard when the volume grows and nobody has protected the routine."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A small firm can survive without a formal routine.
Discipline matters more as transaction volume rises.
Once a routine slips, it is quick and cheap to restore.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz "once it slips, it takes months to rebuild" — o autor discordaria que seja rápido e barato.

items.q: What does the phrase "the audit report nobody wanted to write" suggest?
options: A broken routine eventually produces visible, unwelcome findings
The team enjoys writing detailed reports
Audit reports are optional for small firms
items.why: Inferência: a negligência acaba aparecendo, documentada, num relatório que ninguém queria ter de escrever.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily explicando à equipe como recolocar a rotina nos trilhos. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let me be honest about where we are. Over the last two quarters we grew fast, and somewhere in there the daily work quietly turned into weekly catch-up sessions. Nobody decided that on purpose. It just slipped.

So here is what we are going to do, and please stick with me on this. From Monday, every transaction gets recorded the same day it happens — not on Friday afternoon in one long, painful block. Do reconcile your accounts by end of day every Friday, even a quiet week. And close the books by the fifth working day. No exceptions without a note in the log.

I know this feels heavy at first. It always does. But a steady routine is far lighter than the alternative, which is three of us reconstructing six weeks of receipts the night before an audit. I have lived that once, and I am not doing it again.

One last thing. If the volume gets ahead of us, tell me early. Do not just absorb it silently. Protecting this routine is my job, and I would rather add a person than watch it slip a second time.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: According to Emily, how did the daily work change over the last two quarters?
options: It was handed to an outside firm
It quietly turned into weekly catch-up sessions
items.why: "the daily work quietly turned into weekly catch-up sessions."

items.q: From Monday, when must each transaction be recorded?
items.why: "every transaction gets recorded the same day it happens."

items.q: What is the alternative to a steady routine, in Emily's words?
options: Reconstructing six weeks of receipts the night before an audit
Hiring an external auditor every month
Recording transactions weekly instead of daily
Closing the books twice a month
items.why: "three of us reconstructing six weeks of receipts the night before an audit."

items.q: What does Emily most likely mean by "a steady routine is far lighter than the alternative"?
options: The routine requires fewer software tools
Weekly work is preferable to daily work
Consistent daily effort is easier than a painful last-minute cleanup
The team should reduce the number of accounts
items.why: Inferência: o esforço diário e constante pesa menos do que o resgate desesperado antes da auditoria.

items.q: Why does Emily ask the team to tell her early if the volume gets ahead of them?
options: So she can cancel the audit
So she can move the deadline
Because she plans to reduce the team
Because she would rather add a person than let the routine slip again
items.why: Inferência: ela prefere reforçar a equipe a repetir o colapso da rotina — por isso quer ser avisada cedo.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Bookkeeping is about keeping the operation steady as the company grows." Here, steady means…
items.why: Steady = estável, constante — a operação se mantém firme mesmo com o crescimento.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Please ___ the bank account every Friday, even in a quiet week."
items.why: To reconcile = conciliar — comparar os registros internos com o extrato do banco.

items.q: "Close the books by the fifth working day of the following month." A working day is…
options: the last day of the month
a business day, excluding weekends and holidays
items.why: Working day = dia útil — não conta fins de semana nem feriados.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Every unusual entry is logged as an ___, with a short note explaining it."
items.why: Exception = exceção — algo fora do padrão que precisa ser documentado.

items.q: Supporting receipt is best described as…
options: a signature from the team head
a summary of the monthly accounts
a document that proves and backs up a transaction
a reminder to pay a supplier
items.why: Supporting receipt = recibo de apoio — o comprovante que sustenta o lançamento.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões de finanças. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The routine started to slip once the volume doubled." To slip here means to…
options: gradually break down or fall behind
items.why: To slip = deslizar — a disciplina afrouxa e a rotina vai ficando para trás.

items.q: "The team head has to sign off on every closed month." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new daily process across all desks next week." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, colocar em operação.

items.q: "Two analysts pushed back on the Friday deadline." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "They agreed to record daily, but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.
